name: chamfer-through-a-tray-wall
why: A tray chamfered deeper than its walls, written cut-then-chamfer. OpenCASCADE's chamfer on the cut tray returns a closed solid whose faces run through the pocket, which the self-intersection check refuses (held by a_chamfer_through_the_wall_behind_it_is_refused in backend.rs, on the kernel directly). The chamfer's reach meets the pocket, so the part is built chamfer-then-cut and the pocket breaks out through the chamfer faces: a thin-walled tray with its bottom corners cut open, which print_check is there to judge.
